questions.question: An area model for 5n(n + 12) is one large rectangle with height 5n. Its base is split into two parts: one part is n long and the other part is 12 long. This makes two smaller rectangles. What are the areas of the two smaller rectangles?
questions.explain: Multiply the height 5n by each part of the base: 5n × n = 5n² because n × n = n² (add the exponents), and 5n × 12 = 60n. The 12 must be multiplied by 5n too, not left as 12.

questions.question: An area model shows 6y(y + 11). The whole rectangle has height 6y. Its base is cut into two parts: one part is y long and the other part is 11 long. Which sum shows the areas of the two small rectangles added together?
questions.explain: Each small rectangle is height × its part of the base: 6y × y = 6y² and 6y × 11 = 66y, so the sum is 6y² + 66y. Remember y × y = y², not 2y or y.

questions.question: In an area model the whole rectangle has base 7a. Its height is split into two parts: one part is a tall and the other part is 10 tall. Written as the sum of the two smaller areas, what is the total area of the whole rectangle?
questions.explain: The two parts are 7a × a = 7a² and 7a × 10 = 70a, so the total is 7a² + 70a. The common trap is writing a × a as 2a instead of a².

questions.question: An area model for 5x(x + 12y) has height 5x. The base is split into two parts: a part of length x and a part of length 12y. What are the areas of the two small rectangles?
questions.explain: Height times each part of the base: 5x × x = 5x² and 5x × 12y = 60xy. Both parts of the base get multiplied by 5x, and x × x = x².

questions.question: Expand: −5x(x − 12)
questions.explain: Multiply −5x by each term: −5x × x = −5x² and −5x × (−12) = +60x, so the product is −5x² + 60x. Watch the sign of the second term and remember x × x = x².

questions.question: Expand: (a − 11b)(6a)
questions.explain: Multiply 6a by each term inside: 6a × a = 6a² and 6a × (−11b) = −66ab. The −11b must be multiplied by 6a, not copied down unchanged.

questions.question: A rectangular vegetable bed in a Surrey backyard is 5w metres wide and (w + 10) metres long. Which expression gives its area in square metres?
questions.explain: Area = width × length = 5w(w + 10) = 5w × w + 5w × 10 = 5w² + 50w. A common slip is writing w × w as 2w instead of w².

questions.question: Expand: 5x(x + 12y + 10)
questions.explain: Multiply 5x by all three terms: 5x × x = 5x², 5x × 12y = 60xy and 5x × 10 = 50x. Every term in the bracket gets multiplied, and x × x = x².

questions.question: Priya is designing a rectangular poster for a Kamloops school fair. She lets h stand for the height in centimetres. The width is 5 times the height, and then she decides to make the poster 12 cm wider than that. Which expression gives the area of the poster in cm²?
questions.explain: The width is 5h + 12, so the area is h(5h + 12) = 5h² + 12h. Both terms in the bracket get multiplied by h, and h × h = h², not 2h.

questions.question: A kite is sewn from two identical rectangular panels of fabric. Each panel is 3n cm wide and (n + 50) cm long. Which expression gives the total area of fabric in cm² for both panels?
questions.explain: One panel is 3n(n + 50) = 3n² + 150n, and two panels give 6n² + 300n. Remember n × n = n², and the 50 must be multiplied by 3n as well.

questions.question: Ava expands 2n(n + 7) and writes 2n² + 7. Which statement about her work is correct?
options: Nothing is wrong, because 7 has no n, so it just stays 7.
2n × n should be 4n, not 2n², so it should be 4n + 7.
She must multiply 7 by 2n too, giving 2n² + 14n.
2n × n should be 2n, not 2n², so it should be 2n + 7.
questions.explain: Every term inside the brackets gets multiplied by 2n: 2n × n = 2n² and 2n × 7 = 14n, so 2n(n + 7) = 2n² + 14n. Leaving the 7 alone is the most common error.

questions.question: Noah expands 3x(x + 5). He writes 3x × x = 6x because x × x = 2x, then gets 6x + 15x = 21x. Which statement is correct?
options: He is right: x × x = 2x, so 3x × x = 6x and the total is 21x.
He is wrong: only the x is multiplied by 3x, so it is 3x² + 5.
He is wrong: x × x = x since 1 × 1 = 1, so it is 3x + 15x.
He is wrong: x × x = x², so the product is 3x² + 15x.
questions.explain: x × x means x¹ × x¹ = x² (add the exponents), so 3x(x + 5) = 3x² + 15x. Writing x × x as 2x confuses multiplying with adding, since x + x = 2x.
